67
CO-OWNED PROPERTY
Co-owned property shall be all property rights acquired by work or against payment during the marriage or domestic community of the spouses. Co-owned property of spouses shall also be property acquired on the basis and by means of the co-owned property or the property that arises from such property.
FAMILY', "Country: Slovenia | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 68
68
SPOUSES' SHARES IN CO-OWNED PROPERTY
(1) Co-owned property of spouses shall belong jointly to both spouses. Shares belonging to each spouse shall not be specified in the co-owned property.
(2) A spouse may not dispose of their unspecified share of co-owned property by legal transactions inter vivos, and in particular, they may not expropriate or encumber it.
(3) Items that are part of co-owned property shall be jointly owned by the spouses.
FAMILY", 'Country: Slovenia | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 66
66
LEGAL MARITAL PROPERTY REGIME
A legal marital property regime between spouses shall be a community property regime for the co-owned property of spouses and a separate property regime for the personal property of each spouse.
FAMILY']
response:
In Slovenia, “co‑owned property” (skupna lastnina) is defined as **all property rights that the spouses acquire by work or for consideration during the marriage or their domestic community, as well as any property that is acquired on the basis of, by means of, or that arises from that co‑owned property**[S1].  

The co‑owned property is **jointly owned by the spouses**; the individual shares are not specified, and a spouse may not dispose of their unspecified share by inter‑ vivos legal transactions, nor encumber or expropriate it[S2].  

The legal marital property regime treats this co‑owned property as a **community property regime**, while each spouse’s personal property remains separate[S3].

user_input: When is the community of property between spouses dissolved in Italy?

* by a declaration of absence or presumed death of one spouse,  
* by annulment of the marriage, by dissolution or termination of its civil effects,
